title: The square through and the Jersey twirl carry it
assumes: B1 is the travelling phrase: a balance and square through two with number three, long lines forward, then a Jersey twirl with number four — you end B1 standing where number four was, and B2's ring and partner swing are danced there.
quotes: B1  (8) Interrupted square through 2 [with N3]: (4) N3 neighbor balance (RH)  (4) Square through 2 (N3R;PL)  (4) In long lines, go forward (facing out)  (4) N4 neighbor Jersey twirl
notes: One clause, on the Jersey twirl, so the whole triple shift lands at the end of B1 and A2's N2 and B1's N3 and N4 are all read from the seating the time through started in. **Measured** at six couples: `closure 0.0000 · progressed 68.0000 · reach 19.3787 short · collision 1.085`, against the record's `0.0000 · 20.0000 · 14.3567 · 0.246`. Identical to the pull-by reading on closure, `progressed` and reach at this length and better on collision: what differs between the two is only which sixteen beats are danced in which seating.
